changes.title: Stop the launcher loop
changes.body: If npm skipped Liner's platform package, liner could start copies of itself until stopped. It now stops with a clear message instead.

changes.title: Find a separately installed CLI
changes.body: When the bundled CLI is missing, liner uses another Liner CLI on your PATH, never another copy of the launcher.

intro: liner no longer starts itself in a loop when its platform package is missing, and it finds a separately installed Liner CLI on your PATH.

changes.title: Install the browser only when you ask
changes.body: Repair never downloads it. Press i to install JS rendering: about 100 MB to download, about 220 MB on disk.

changes.title: Read every source note
changes.body: Review Draft Sources shows each Source's full agent note, how much of it the agents could read, and its section and kind.

changes.title: Edit long text
changes.body: The synthesis and Project Skill editors accept new lines at any length, and the approve action stays on screen.

changes.title: Continue without failed sources
changes.body: After you review the failed Sources, press l to create the Operating Layer from the usable ones.

changes.title: Follow the latest improvement status
changes.body: An applied improvement pass is no longer offered again, and its gaps are shown in plain words.

changes.title: New default models
changes.body: OpenAI Auto runs Sol 6.1 at Medium. Claude runs Sonnet 5.5 at Medium, with Opus 5.5 and a Thinking effort setting.

intro: You decide which sources to trust and what the synthesis says, with the agents' notes on screen. JS rendering installs only when you ask, and Sol 6.1 and Sonnet 5.5 are the new defaults.

changes.title: Resume interrupted research
changes.body: Reopen a Project after an interrupted agent run or a validation failure to return to the last saved review or build step. Partial work stays marked as incomplete.

changes.title: Preserve approved sources
changes.body: Sources you already accepted keep their IDs when Assembly adds evaluation details. Pending Assembly is shown as the next action when needed.

changes.title: Save improvement decisions
changes.body: Improve Corpus decisions survive restarts. Applied recommendations stay resolved, and the audit keeps the original gap as history.

changes.title: Clarify confirmations
changes.body: Source and synthesis transitions show ordinary confirmation messages. Recoverable Project deletion keeps focus on the exact confirmation step.

intro: Interrupted research resumes from its saved checkpoint. Approved sources keep their IDs through Assembly, and Improve Corpus decisions survive restarts with a visible audit record.

changes.title: Review maintenance through Liner Core
changes.body: Project and Source changes use the same CLI-owned snapshots, plans, risk checks, and receipts. Higher-risk operations wait for approval of the exact preview.

changes.title: Approve sources and synthesis separately
changes.body: Source review shows what will be added and what stays unchanged. A separate synthesis approval records the decision and starts compile.

changes.title: Recover deleted Projects
changes.body: Delete Project asks for the exact name and previews a move to Liner Trash. The folder leaves the active library while its files and Project ID remain recoverable.

changes.title: Maintain with Codex or Claude Code
changes.body: Optional Maintenance Adapters route changes through the installed CLI. Inspect, install, update, and remove commands preserve content outside Liner-managed files and blocks.

changes.title: Load clearer Project instructions
changes.body: Generated root SKILL.md files give compatible AI assistants a concise entry point, load order, and completion criteria. Detailed operating rules remain in LINER.md.

changes.title: Recover blocked sources
changes.body: Browser fallback can recover some security-checkpoint responses. Recovered material refreshes the affected evaluation steps, and ordinary curator notes no longer appear as compile warnings.

changes.title: Simplify browser setup
changes.body: JavaScript rendering setup offers one install action and shows a loader while Playwright Chromium is downloading.

intro: Source selection and synthesis now receive separate approval before compile. Maintenance previews Project and Source changes, requests approval when required, and saves a receipt, including for recoverable Project deletion.

changes.title: Read compile results first
changes.body: Compile opens with a compact summary. Source review brings errors, retryable custom sources, and recovered content to the top.

changes.title: Repair custom sources
changes.body: Retry unavailable custom web or YouTube sources, install browser rendering when needed, and review recovered material before continuing.

changes.title: Keep repair work in context
changes.body: Adding replacement material returns to compile. Recovered local sources remain available for the next research build.

changes.title: Continue with usable partial results
changes.body: After reviewing warnings, a usable MIXTAPE.md can proceed to AI instruction creation. Completed Projects open LINER.md as their next action.

intro: Compile summarizes the result before showing source details. It guides recovery for blocked web and YouTube sources and lets reviewed, usable partial results continue to AI instruction writing.

changes.title: Open the Go terminal UI
changes.body: Running liner or npx linersh opens the terminal UI for creating, opening, and managing local Projects.

changes.title: Install through npm
changes.body: The linersh package includes the terminal UI and matching platform CLI binaries. Normal use needs no separate Python setup.

changes.title: Create AI instructions
changes.body: After the research is ready, Create Operating Layer writes LINER.md, root SKILL.md, and liner.yaml from the saved artifacts. The files describe how to use the evidence and respect its boundaries.

changes.title: Carry research into the method
changes.body: Generated instructions use the saved synthesis, quality checks, source roles, and capability patterns to guide work with the Project.

intro: The first complete Project-builder release uses the Go terminal UI by default. The npm package includes the CLI and terminal UI, and completed folders carry AI instructions.

changes.title: Extract browser-downloaded PDFs
changes.body: When browser fallback receives a PDF download, Liner captures the file and runs PDF text extraction.

intro: Browser fallback can capture PDF downloads and extract their text.

changes.title: Recognize remote PDFs
changes.body: Web responses identified as PDFs use PDF extraction, so raw PDF bytes no longer become source text.

changes.title: Refetch unusable cache entries
changes.body: Cached content that resembles a bad PDF extraction, an empty fallback, or cookie-only output is discarded and fetched again.

changes.title: Detect empty pages
changes.body: Empty JavaScript shells trigger browser fallback. Cookie-consent-only output is marked unavailable.

changes.title: Explain partial compiles
changes.body: Compile reports the count of usable sources separately from unavailable source files.

intro: Source fetching checks remote PDFs, empty JavaScript pages, cookie-only output, and stale cache entries. Partial compiles report usable and unavailable sources separately.

changes.title: Improve terminal scrolling
changes.body: Final responses and long compile source lists use internal scrolling areas that fit the terminal.

changes.title: Set up browser rendering
changes.body: First-run setup offers optional Playwright Chromium installation. Compile also surfaces missing browser support for JavaScript-only pages.

changes.title: Keep usable compile results accessible
changes.body: Partial compiles remain available with warnings. Opening a current result avoids rerunning compile; r explicitly retries it.

changes.title: Recover from HTML extraction errors
changes.body: A text fallback can retain a source with a warning when the primary HTML extractor fails.

changes.title: Remove local state for a clean reinstall
changes.body: The new uninstall command removes Liner configuration and source cache, shared Playwright browsers, and npm npx execution cache.

intro: This release improves terminal scrolling, JavaScript rendering setup, partial compiles, and clean reinstall testing.

changes.title: Find the bundled research skill
changes.body: npm installs locate the included skill bundle more reliably and report the checked paths when it is missing.

changes.title: Add a Windows install path
changes.body: Windows x64 receives a native platform package alongside macOS and Linux.

changes.title: Configure models by phase
changes.body: Discovery and evaluation can use a cheaper configured model, while other research phases use the runner default. A rejected model setting warns and retries once with the default.

changes.title: Detect an unresponsive runner
changes.body: A runner that emits no output within 15 seconds produces a clear failure with retry and switch-runner options.

changes.title: Report usage accurately
changes.body: Run summaries keep token counts and remove the unsupported dollar-cost estimate.

intro: Fresh npm installs find the bundled research skill more reliably. Windows x64 gains a platform install path alongside macOS and Linux.

changes.title: Report both installed versions
changes.body: The version command reports the terminal UI package and bundled CLI core together, or only the terminal UI version when the core cannot be resolved.

changes.title: Keep version labels consistent
changes.body: The header and startup screen read the package version directly.

intro: Version output reports both the installed terminal UI package and the CLI core.

changes.title: Simplify the research hub
changes.body: The hub shows one status summary with a phase checklist. In this release, compile is the completion milestone.

changes.title: Streamline import and navigation
changes.body: Import detects .mixtape files in the current folder and opens the imported research hub. Screen actions and back navigation become more consistent.

changes.title: Fit lists and responses to the terminal
changes.body: Project lists and final responses use bounded viewports to reduce wrapping and repeated scrollback.

changes.title: Improve runner reliability
changes.body: Claude runs avoid a known compaction error and use an isolated MCP configuration for the research workflow.

changes.title: Remove unsupported cost estimates
changes.body: Run summaries show token counts without an invented dollar figure.

intro: The terminal hub gains one status view, clearer navigation, and more accurate run summaries.

changes.title: Bundle the research skill
changes.body: The npm package includes the research skill needed for AI-assisted task clarification.

changes.title: Improve terminal readability
changes.body: Updated colors, explicit text contrast, and a cleaner startup logo improve legibility.

changes.title: Refine navigation and feedback
changes.body: Back navigation avoids a loop, result notes stay visible, and the o shortcut opens the research folder.

changes.title: Reduce scrollback artifacts
changes.body: The terminal app uses the alternate-screen buffer and clears the screen after a run completes.

intro: The first update after the npm terminal UI release improves startup, colors, navigation, and folder opening.

changes.title: Run the terminal UI from npm
changes.body: npx linersh opens the terminal UI on clean machines. After a global install, liner opens the same interface.

changes.title: Keep CLI commands available
changes.body: The installed command supports setup-js, compile, share, and status alongside the terminal UI.

intro: The interactive terminal UI becomes available through npm on clean machines.
